Installation was smooth and I had no issues. I do have a separate /opt and /home partition because this is a release candidate.

The interface is fine (XFCE) and the initial color scheme not horrifically painful on the eyes.

Installed items are pretty much the default XFCE installation, so you'll need to do some configuration if you're coming from a different DE.

I encountered one real issue with Devuan so far and two minor irritants that were easily resolved.

Synaptic did not launch from the Applications Menu for me(I just opened a terminal and sudoed it to start in RC1) I got around to fixing it today. The .desktop short cut entry was:

Exec=synaptic-pkexec

and it now works with:

Exec=gksudo synaptic-pkexec

So if you are experimenting, you may need to make changes.

The pain point is a sound issue that is caused by hdmi output. (I just updated to the next RC version and at a cursory glance, it seems to persist, I just upgraded and my playtime is over for the day, so I'll need to explore tomorrow or next week)

http://forums.debian.net/viewtopic.php?t=110572#p525601

https://dev1galaxy.org/viewtopic.php?id=27

This above forum posts discuss and explain how to fix the sound issue and the cause.

The repos seem to be reasonable for a RC distro.

One thing to be aware of is that they have Firefox ESR 45 in the repos. If you intend to use add ons (hopefully you are) the FireFox add-on pages will give you crap about your browser being out of date for some add-ons due to their upcoming changes.

Firefox release page below: https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/organizations/all/

I elected to remove the Firefox-ESR package and run FireFox 52 by putting it in my opt folder (for those interested that may not know how, you can just move everything to the opt folder and create a .desktop entry to make a GUI short cut).

This below is intended for anyone who may not know how to do this that may be reading, but are curious. It used to drive me mad when people would chat about something that was common knowledge among themselves, but as a noob, John Snow knew more than me (and still probably does). Also, please note this is not the best way to do things for most packages. If you elect to do this make sure whatever you move there auto updates or provides update messages and can run (obviously). I'm experimenting with Devuan and am unsure if it'll be a long term distro for me or not so I'm also taking some shortcuts that may or may not be appropriate in the long run. Finally, this is a release candidate distro so it's possible that an unexpected error can break all the things on the next upgrade and cause me to have to start over at scratch anyway so I partitioned my ssd to within an inch of its life so I don't have to repeat as much work (hopefully).

Assuming you extracted it to FireFox52

sudo mv ~/FireFox52 /opt

To make the short cut in the menu:

cd /usr/share/applications

You will see a lot of .desktop files. This is where you can create or modify a shortcut for XFCE.

vim firefox.desktop

The entry will look something similar to below (this works, I just copied the chromium entry and changed a few things):

[Desktop Entry]
Name=FireFox
GenericName=Internet Browser
Exec=/opt/firefox52/firefox %U
Icon=/opt/firefox52/browser/icons/mozicon128.png
Terminal=false
Type=Application
StartupNotify=false
Categories=Network;WebBrowser
MimeType=text/html;text/xml;application/xhtml_xml;x-scheme-handler/http;x-scheme-handler/https;
